newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures traded in a narrow range on Monday, hit early in the session by German pessimism then helped late in the day by U.S. optimism to settle little changed.
Traders said the session was calm and only 44,800 September bond contracts changed hands, the third lowest volume this year.
Both the French holiday season and caution ahead of a series of potentially market moving U.S. statistics later in the week were blamed for the lacklustre performance.
Traders said the contract looked destined to remain trapped between 130.34 and 130.88 unless shaken out of its current torpor by one of the other major bond markets.

With U.S. Treasuries buoyed by fading fears of an early interest rate rise and a strong dollar, traders said the main risk to the current environment would be if stronger-than-expected U.S. data revived rate hike concerns.
In Europe, the main cloud on the horizon remained in Germany, with lingering concerns the decline in the mark against the dollar could spur the Bundesbank into raising money market rates.
"The big international investors are looking at Asia and we're on holiday," said one trader in Paris.

PIBOR contracts slipped with Euromarks as both the mark and the franc fell against the dollar. While few feared the German central bank would actually act in the near-term, one trader said the September contract looked likely to remain capped around 96.55 until after the next Bundesbank council meeting.
The franc fell as low as 6.2340 against the dollar, its lowest level since July 1991, and weakened slightly against the mark to 3.3714.

PIBOR contracts in the second half of 1998 continued to underperform the front months. September 1998 slipped two basis points while September 1997 recovered from its early decline to settle unchanged.
The average yield on 13-week Treasury bills rose at auction on Monday to 3.26 percent from 3.24 percent last week.
